input_analysis: Repository scan found no existing product web app; the pilot therefore uses an isolated Python standard-library HTTP example to avoid unrelated stack drift.
key_decisions: Use Python http.server and unittest so the pilot adds no external runtime dependency.
Read LOGIN_HOMEPAGE_USERNAME and LOGIN_HOMEPAGE_PASSWORD from environment variables to keep credentials deployment-owned.
Store sessions server-side in memory and expose only an opaque HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie to the client.
Use real HTTP requests in tests so QA evidence follows the same boundary as a user journey.

key_scenarios: anonymous redirect, login form, valid login, homepage, logout, and stale cookie paths are verified through real localhost HTTP requests
tradeoff_points: standard-library HTTP avoids unrelated stack introduction while preserving journey-level evidence

key_scenarios: login credentials are supplied through environment variables instead of hardcoded values
tradeoff_points: environment variables are sufficient for the pilot and avoid a config service dependency

key_scenarios: logout clears server-side session state and stale cookies cannot access the homepage
tradeoff_points: in-memory sessions keep the pilot isolated while exercising auth-like behavior

option_analysis.summary: Use an isolated Python standard-library app for the pilot.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Lower product realism than a full browser app, but provides deterministic real HTTP evidence without stack introduction.

option_analysis.summary: Introduce a frontend framework and build a browser app.
option_analysis.tradeoff: More UI realism, but adds dependency and setup noise unrelated to standard-chain handoff validation.

option_analysis.summary: Only write canonical artifacts without executable code.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Exercises validators but fails the direct-evidence requirement for feature delivery.

interfaces.contract_summary: GET /login renders the form; POST /login validates configured credentials and returns a session cookie on success.
GET / redirects anonymous users and renders homepage content for active session cookies.
POST /logout removes the server-side token and sends an expired session cookie.

migration_plan: Add isolated example app files; no migration touches existing runtime or shared skill code.
verification_plan: Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_login_homepage_app.py' for real HTTP acceptance.
Run py_compile for app and test files.
Run standard-chain phase, readiness, and replay validators against docs/login-homepage-pilot/phase-1.
rollback_plan: Remove examples/login_homepage_app, tests/test_login_homepage_app.py, and docs/login-homepage-pilot if the pilot gate fails.

modules.name: login homepage example app
modules.responsibility: serve login, homepage, and logout flows with environment-owned credentials and server-side session state

data_architecture.summary: Session tokens are stored in process-local memory; credentials are read from environment variables; no durable storage or external datasource is introduced.
storage_decisions: Use in-memory session storage because the pilot validates standard-chain flow, not production session durability.
data_flows: POST /login validates configured credentials, creates an opaque session token, and GET / uses the token to render the homepage.
data_architecture.consistency_strategy: Logout removes the server-side token before sending an expired cookie so stale cookies fail closed.

cross_cutting_concerns.decision: Use environment-owned credentials, opaque HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookies, and server-side session invalidation.
Missing config, invalid form length, invalid credentials, unknown sessions, and unknown routes return readable failures.
Invalid login attempts remain visible in default HTTP access logs.
Credentials are supplied by LOGIN_HOMEPAGE_USERNAME and LOGIN_HOMEPAGE_PASSWORD environment variables.

verification_mapping.design_validation: Real HTTP tests cover anonymous redirect, login form, valid login, invalid login, homepage, logout, stale cookie, and access-log behavior.
verification_mapping.test_obligation: Run login-homepage HTTP acceptance and negative-path tests.

verification_mapping.design_validation: Standard-chain validators must accept the upgraded canonical design, tests, readiness, and replay artifacts.
verification_mapping.test_obligation: Run phase, readiness, and replay validators for docs/login-homepage-pilot/phase-1.

verification_mapping.design_validation: Review, QA, consistency audit, signoff, and user decision artifacts must resolve through the active registry.

impact_scope.impact: Adds isolated login, homepage, logout, credential config, session cookie, and stale-cookie handling.

planning_constraints.description: Keep the pilot on Python standard-library HTTP and unittest without introducing external runtime dependencies.
Do not hardcode login credentials; keep them environment-owned.

risks.description: In-memory sessions are not durable and are suitable only for the isolated pilot.
Missing or hardcoded credentials would weaken the pilot auth boundary.

risk_response.architecture_response: Keep sessions explicitly scoped to the local pilot and verify logout invalidates server-side state.
risk_response.escalation_path: If durable sessions are required, return to design before implementation.

risk_response.architecture_response: Require credentials from environment variables and test missing/invalid configuration behavior.
risk_response.escalation_path: If credential management expands, escalate to design for config architecture.
